meta.title: DFX BTC Taro Wallet — Handbook
meta.description: Illustrated guide to the DFX BTC Taro Wallet: create a wallet, receive and send bitcoin, secure your backup, use Lightning.
meta.lede: This guide walks through the app picture by picture, in the order the steps appear in the wallet. Every image is a real capture from the app.

chapters.title: Getting started
chapters.summary: Open the app for the first time and create a wallet.
chapters.intro: On first launch the app creates a wallet on your device. The keys stay on the phone. DFX has no access to them and cannot restore a lost wallet. That is why the disclaimer comes first, and why the step after creating a wallet is always the backup.

chapters.title: Receiving bitcoin
chapters.summary: Show an address and accept a payment.
chapters.intro: To receive, the wallet shows an address as a code. Whoever pays scans that code. Amount and description are optional and only help you recognise the payment later. The wallet creates a new address for every payment. That is intended, and it is good for your privacy.

chapters.title: Sending bitcoin
chapters.summary: Make a payment, usually with the scanner.
chapters.intro: Sending needs the address of the recipient. The scanner is the easiest way: it reads the code of the other party and fills in address and amount by itself. A payment in bitcoin cannot be recalled once sent. So check the address and the amount once more before you confirm.

chapters.title: Backup and security
chapters.summary: Secure the recovery phrase and export the wallet.
chapters.intro: The recovery phrase of twelve words is the wallet. Whoever holds it holds the money. Whoever loses it and loses the device has lost the money. It belongs on paper in a safe place, not in a photo, not in a chat, not in the cloud. In this chapter the phrase and the code for the export are blacked out, because otherwise they would sit in a public repository.

chapters.title: Lightning
chapters.summary: Small amounts, instantly and at very low cost.
chapters.intro: Lightning is a second layer on top of bitcoin for small, fast payments. New users create Lightning (Spark) with a tap on the row in the overview. Buying and selling are there as on the other wallets; there is no payment card. The Lightning address lives on Breez. For larger amounts the wallet on the blockchain is the right place.

chapters.title: More wallets: adding and importing
chapters.summary: A wallet across three devices, another wallet for Lightning, reading in an existing wallet.
chapters.intro: Besides the wallet from the first launch you can create more: a wallet spread across three devices, where two of them approve every payment, or Lightning (Spark) with a tap on the row in the overview. There is no choice of provider. A wallet created elsewhere can be read in from the recovery phrase, a private key or a code.

chapters.title: Settings
chapters.summary: Currency, language, security, network and tools.
chapters.intro: The settings let you change the displayed currency and the language, put a lock on the app and change the server of Electrum in use. The tools are meant for rare occasions, for instance to check whether an address belongs to your own wallet.

01-onboarding/01-start.title: Disclaimer on first launch
01-onboarding/01-start.text: Before the first wallet the app points out that it keeps the keys itself: they live on the device, not with DFX.

01-onboarding/02-wallet-uebersicht.title: The overview after setup
01-onboarding/02-wallet-uebersicht.text: Once created, the overview shows your balance and your wallets. Every other path starts here.

01-onboarding/03-mitteilungen-berechtigu.title: Permission for notifications
01-onboarding/03-mitteilungen-berechtigu.text: The first time you open “Receive”, the phone asks for permission to send notifications. That is how the app reports incoming payments.

02-wallet/01-uebersicht.title: Overview of the wallet
02-wallet/01-uebersicht.text: The detail page of a wallet with balance, transactions and the buttons for receiving and sending.

02-wallet/02-backup-erklaerung.title: What the recovery phrase is for
02-wallet/02-backup-erklaerung.text: Before showing them, the app explains what the twelve words mean and why nobody else may see them.

02-wallet/03-signieren-verifizieren.title: Signing and checking a message
02-wallet/03-signieren-verifizieren.text: The private key can sign a message. That proves an address belongs to your own wallet.

02-wallet/04-onchain-transaktionen.title: Transactions of the wallet
02-wallet/04-onchain-transaktionen.text: The list of all incoming and outgoing payments of this wallet.

02-wallet/05-adressen.title: List of addresses
02-wallet/05-adressen.text: All addresses of the wallet, with balance and usage. New addresses for receiving appear automatically.

02-wallet/06-export-backup.title: Export and backup
02-wallet/06-export-backup.text: The wallet can be exported as a code to move it to another device. The code contains the key and belongs in front of nobody else's camera.

02-wallet/07-xpub.title: Public key
02-wallet/07-xpub.text: The public key lets you follow incoming payments without being able to spend. It does reveal every address of the wallet.

02-wallet/08-wiederherstellungsphrase.text: The recovery phrase. Write it on paper, keep the order, store it safely. Blacked out here for the handbook.

04-empfangen-senden/02-senden.text: The scanner reads the code of the recipient and takes over address and amount.

06-wallet-hinzufuegen/01-multi-device.text: One wallet spread across three devices: two of them approve every payment. That protects you from a single lost device costing you the money.

06-wallet-hinzufuegen/02-lightning-spark.text: A tap on “Add” in this row creates Lightning (Spark). There is no further choice.
